messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
అలా నన్ను విశ్రాంతి లేని మృగంగా చేసింది, అది నన్ను ఎదుర్కొంటూ క్రమంగా నన్ను సూర్యుడు నిశ్శబ్దంగా ఉన్న చోటకు నెట్టింది.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Telugu) | Back‑Translation (Eng.) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|--------| | tal | demonstrative “such” introducing the beast | **అలా** | such | OK | | mi | 1st‑person singular object “me” | **నన్ను** | me | OK | | fece | causative past “made” | **చేసింది** | made (caused) | OK | | la | definite article (feminine) | — (article omitted) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | bestia | “beast” (creature lacking peace) | **మృగంగా** | as a beast | OK | | sanza | preposition “without” | **లేని** | without | OK | | pace | “repose / peace” | **విశ్రాంతి** | repose | OK | | che | relative pronoun “that” introducing clause | **అది** | that (the beast) | OK | | venendomi | gerund “coming on against me” (approaching) | **ఎదుర్కొంటూ** | confronting / coming against | OK | | ’ncontro | preposition “against” (direction) | — (sense folded into **ఎదుర్కొంటూ**) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | a (1st) | part of idiom “a poco a poco” (incremental) | **క్రమంగా** (combined) | gradually / little‑by‑little | **UNNECESSARY** | | poco (1st) | “little” (degree) | **క్రమంగా** (combined) | gradually | **UNNECESSARY** | | a (2nd) | part of idiom “a poco a poco” (incremental) | **క్రమంగా** (combined) | gradually | **UNNECESSARY** | | poco (2nd) | “little” (degree) | **క్రమంగా** (combined) | gradually | **UNNECESSARY** | | mi (2nd) | 1st‑person singular object “me” | **నన్ను** | me | OK | | ripigneva | imperfect “was pushing back” | **నెట్టింది** | pushed (back) | OK | | là | adverb “there / thither” | **చోటకు** | to that place | OK | | dove | relative adverb “where” | **చోటకు** (as part of relative clause) | where (to the place) | OK | | ’l | definite article “the” (before *sol*) | — (article omitted) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | sol | noun “Sun” | **సూర్యుడు** | Sun | OK | | tace | verb “is silent” | **నిశ్శబ్దంగా ఉన్న** | is silent | OK |
### Summary of Issues - **UNNECESSARY** items (articles or prepositions that Telugu naturally omits or that are merged into a single lexical item): `la`, `’ncontro`, both occurrences of `a` and `poco` in the idiom, and `’l`. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** problems were detected; all required meanings are conveyed in the Telugu translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
